content.text: The text is a nineteenth-century miscellany combining polemical history, riddles, advertisements, agricultural advice, market reports, fiction, and Canadian history. It recounts alleged horrors in the Spanish and Roman Inquisitions, convent confinement, and anti-Catholic warnings. Numerous jokes and word puzzles follow, alongside poultry, beekeeping, farming, commerce, and product advertisements. A historical section describes the Lower Canada rebellions: battles at St Denis, St Charles, Moore’s Corners, St Eustache, and Odelltown; executions, burnings, and Lord Durham’s arrival in Quebec, amnesty, resignation, and influential report. Fiction follows John Smith’s attempts to help Miss Flora and the Blaisdells, while concealing that he is wealthy Stanley Fulton. Money causes family trouble, but losses prompt reform. Finally, Smith returns to Miss Maggie, reveals his love, and proposes marriage; she reciprocates, though their identities and Fulton’s fortune remain unresolved.
